title: Operator-Space Entanglement Entropy in Random Fermionic Gaussian Dynamics
authors: Pablo Bayona-Pena, Elena Gramellini, Lorenzo Piroli
abstract: We study the von Neumann operator-space entanglement entropy (OSEE) of initial product operators evolved under random gaussian dynamics, as modeled by a Brownian SYK$_2$ model. By exploiting a mapping to a domain-wall melting problem, we derive an exact expression for the time-dependent bipartite OSEE in the thermodynamic limit, and obtain an analytic characterization of the corresponding gaussian Page curve emerging at late times. Our results build on recent work on the entanglement dynamics in the all-to-all quantum simple exclusion process, leveraging tools from RMT, including the Coulomb-gas approach and a mapping to the free Jacobi process. Finally, based on our results, we discuss the possibility of relating the OSEE with non-gaussianity measures in the Heisenberg picture.
summary: This paper calculates the Operator-Space Entanglement Entropy (OSEE) for fermions evolving under random Gaussian dynamics modeled by a Brownian SYK2 Hamiltonian. By mapping the problem to a domain-wall melting problem and employing Random Matrix Theory, the authors derive an exact, analytic formula for the time-dependent OSEE. This work provides a rigorous tool to characterize entanglement dynamics in complex, non-equilibrium quantum systems.
main_problem: The study focuses on deriving and characterizing the time-dependent von Neumann operator-space entanglement entropy (OSEE) for initial product operators evolving under random Gaussian dynamics.
main_result: The authors derived an exact, analytic expression for the time-dependent bipartite OSEE in the thermodynamic limit and characterized the emerging Gaussian Page curve.
method: The analysis employs advanced tools from Random Matrix Theory (RMT), including the Coulomb-gas approach and mapping the problem to a domain-wall melting problem, leading to solutions expressed via the resolvent function.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by fermionic dynamics governed by a Brownian SYK2 model, involving Majorana strings and random Gaussian evolution.
key_observables: Operator-Space Entanglement Entropy (OSEE), $	ext{Sop}(\ell)$, and the corresponding Gaussian Page curve.
important_parameters: The thermodynamic limit ($L 	o \infty$), and the time evolution parameter $t$.
main_assumptions: The initial state is assumed to be unentangled (a product of local Majorana operators).

paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the OSEE, mapping the dynamics to a solvable problem (domain-wall melting), utilizing RMT techniques (moment evolution, resolvent formulation), and finally deriving the exact quadrature expression for the entropy.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Stationary gaussian Page curves for NS = 500 Haar samples at L = 80, left panel, and L = 180 for the right panel. The numerical Haar–SO(L) data (dots) are compared with the Coulomb-gas prediction (bold curves) Eq. (42). Both panels also show the fully Haar-random non-gaussian reference used in the numerical study, emphasizing that gaussian scrambling produces a distinct, θ-dependent family of Page curves.

Figure 2. Numerical comparison of the real (β = 1) operator Jacobi dynamics and the complex (β = 2) state Jacobi dynamics with the common thermodynamic limit, for the balanced bipartition q = θ = 1/2 (left), q = 0.6, θ = 0.3 (middle), q = 0.8, θ = 0.4 (right). Circles denote the state entanglement obtained from complex random-unitary evolution of a DW state, while squares denote the OSEE generated by the gaussian evolution of a Majorana string. Lower row: finite size deviations of the entropy-density dynamics; the black curve is the thermodynamic prediction Eqs. (62, 69) .
